items.followUp: Why do ionic compounds have high melting points?

rubric.why: Identifies the physical state of ionic compounds.
rubric.description: States that ionic compounds are solids.
rubric.how: Award for clearly stating that ionic compounds are solid at room temperature.

rubric.why: Explains what holds the ions in fixed positions.
rubric.description: Attributes their solid state to strong attraction between oppositely charged ions.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the strong ionic attraction that holds the ions together.

modelAnswer: Ionic compounds are solids because strong electrostatic forces of attraction between oppositely charged ions hold them in fixed positions in a crystal lattice.

items.followUp: Define diffusion and give one example from everyday life.

rubric.why: Defines diffusion as particle spreading from a region of higher concentration to lower concentration.
rubric.description: Defines diffusion using the movement of particles down a concentration gradient.
rubric.how: Award for the direction of movement from higher to lower concentration.

rubric.why: Shows the concept through a valid example.
rubric.how: Award for an example such as perfume spreading through air or ink spreading in water.

modelAnswer: Diffusion is the spontaneous movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration.
For example, the smell of perfume spreads through a room by diffusion.

items.followUp: What is evaporation? Name one factor, other than surface area, that increases its rate.

rubric.why: Identifies evaporation as a change from liquid to vapour at the surface.
rubric.description: Defines evaporation as the escape of surface particles from a liquid into vapour.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning the liquid-to-vapour change and the surface.

rubric.why: States the effect of increasing the exposed surface area.
rubric.description: Explains that a larger surface area increases the rate of evaporation.
rubric.how: Award for stating that evaporation becomes faster as surface area increases.

modelAnswer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour from its surface.
Increasing the surface area of a liquid increases the rate of evaporation.

items.followUp: Define allotropy and name two allotropes of oxygen.

rubric.why: Includes the defining features of allotropy.
rubric.description: Defines allotropy as the existence of an element in different forms in the same physical state.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the forms are of the same element and in the same physical state.

rubric.why: Provides a valid pair of allotropes.
rubric.how: Award for a correct pair, such as diamond and graphite or oxygen and ozone.

modelAnswer: Allotropy is the existence of an element in two or more different forms in the same physical state.
Diamond and graphite are allotropes of carbon.

items.followUp: What is a solute? Give an example of an aqueous solution.

rubric.why: Identifies an aqueous solution as a solution or mixture.
rubric.description: States that an aqueous solution is a solution (homogeneous mixture).
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as a solution or homogeneous mixture.

rubric.why: Identifies water as the solvent in an aqueous solution.
rubric.description: States that water acts as the solvent.
rubric.how: Award for specifying that the solvent is water.

modelAnswer: An aqueous solution is a homogeneous mixture in which water acts as the solvent.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a dilute solution and a concentrated solution.

rubric.why: Describes the role of the solute.
rubric.description: States that a solute is the substance dissolved in a solvent.
rubric.how: Award for correctly identifying what the solute does.

rubric.why: Describes the role of the solvent.
rubric.description: States that a solvent is the substance that dissolves the solute.
rubric.how: Award for correctly identifying what the solvent does.

modelAnswer: A solute is the substance that is dissolved in a solvent.
A solvent is the substance that dissolves the solute.

items.followUp: Write two chemical properties of non-metals.

rubric.why: Gives a valid chemical reaction of metals with oxygen.
rubric.description: States that metals react with oxygen to form metal oxides.
rubric.how: Award for the property and a correctly identified product.

rubric.why: Gives a valid chemical reaction of metals with acids.
rubric.description: States that many metals react with dilute acids to form a salt and hydrogen gas.
rubric.how: Award for the property and the formation of hydrogen gas.

modelAnswer: Metals react with oxygen to form metal oxides; for example, 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.
Many metals react with dilute acids to form a salt and hydrogen gas; for example, Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂.

items.followUp: Write two physical properties of metals.

rubric.why: States a physical property common to many non-metals.
rubric.description: States that non-metals are generally poor conductors of heat or electricity.
rubric.how: Award for either valid conductivity property.

rubric.why: States another physical property common to non-metals.
rubric.description: Gives a valid property such as dullness, brittleness, or lack of malleability or ductility.
rubric.how: Award for any one valid second property.

modelAnswer: Non-metals are generally poor conductors of heat and electricity.
Solid non-metals are usually brittle and are not malleable or ductile.
